summary: Intermittent cross-region egress to us-east after enabling strict EU residency; TLS handshake and p95 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent requests egressing to us-east after they enabled strict EU residency on 2026-03-09. The symptom is periodic p95/p99 latency and TLS handshake delays (~150-450ms extra) for traffic that should remain in eu-west-1. Impact:
- Customer production traffic for Finova Pay (payments flows) observed p95 latency spikes impacting user-facing flows.
- Occurs ~1-2 times per hour, lasting 30-90s windows.
Environment:
- Customer: Finova Pay (enterprise, private deployment with strict residency flag enabled)
- Platform: Redwood hosted control plane + private VPC egress in eu-west-1
- Affected model endpoints: rw-instruct-7b, gpt-4o-mini
Steps to reproduce (as customer observed):
1) Send a steady request stream pinned to eu-west-1 with strict residency enabled.
2) Watch p95 latency in their application metrics and our API logs.
3) When spike occurs, look at request egress metadata: some requests contain us-east-1 egress path.
Logs/snippets from customer:
- Example trace id: trace-20260310-11:06:03-fp1
- Client-side observed latency jump from 120ms p95 to 560ms p95 for 45s window.
- Customer-side TLS logs show additional handshake RTTs during window.

Requested:
- Why are a subset of requests leaving eu-west after strict residency is enabled?
- Are control-plane events (cert rotation, LB re-registration) causing temporary loss of residency stickiness?
- What mitigations can be applied to avoid user-facing latency spikes?

That can flip the residency lock when probes re-register. Correlating cert-rotation schedule with incident windows.

The change introduced a fallback path for healthcheck probes when an AZ loses capacity; in rare cases this fallback picks cross-region egress. Rolling back that change in a canary to confirm.

investigation_notes:
Observations and evidence:
- Control-plane logs (2026-03-10 03:10:22 UTC) show ALB target group re-registration for the customer's dedicated pool during cert rotation.
- DNS records TTL for residency lock are 30s; we observed a small window where control-plane healthchecks returned from fallback subnet IPs reported in us-east.
- Healthcheck probe workflow (post-PR#8123) attempts local AZ probe, then regional fallback. The fallback path incorrectly used a region-agnostic egress bucket which currently prefers us-east when local pool capacity is low.
- The residency lock state machine will re-evaluate egress candidate on successful healthcheck; if the first successful probe comes from a us-east egress IP, the lock flips to us-east for a short window until subsequent eu-west probes re-establish.
- TLS handshake timing: when egress hops to us-east, client TLS renegotiation and extra routing add ~180-400ms to p95 depending on customer proximity to eu-west.
- Incidence frequency correlates with our cert rotation schedule (every ~8 hours for canary targets) and with brief AZ capacity pressure.
Hypotheses considered and rejected:
- DNS cache on customer side alone: rejected because platform logs show outbound egress IPs from our side change during windows.
- Model runtime causing fallback: rejected; multiple models and endpoints affected simultaneously, pattern matches control-plane events.
Evidence links:
- Control-plane event stream: https://logs.redwood.internal/event/20260310/03:10:22
- Healthcheck trace for trace-20260310-11:06:03-fp1: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/trace-20260310-11:06:03-fp1
resolution:
Workarounds and fixes applied:
- Short-term workaround: Coordinated with customer to disable strict residency (not ideal for compliance) or schedule maintenance windows during our cert rotation. Customer chose a maintenance window for full patch.
- Mitigation performed: Rolled back PR#8123 behavior in eu-west canary pool to prevent cross-region fallback egress for healthchecks. Observed no recurrence in canary for 24 hours.
- Planned permanent fix: Update probe routing logic to bind healthcheck/probe egress to the same residency lock as the customer pool (control-plane change). Add a guard that prevents the residency lock from flipping on a single probe success from a different egress region. Create INT ticket to change probe subnet allocation and cert rotation phasing.
Follow-ups and action items:
- INT-2410: Rework probe subnet assignment and enforce egress-region affinity for healthchecks (assigned to Platform Eng).
- Create rollout plan to apply rollback and patch to all EU pools outside peak windows (scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC with Finova Pay permission).
- Add automated alerting: detect probe-origin region mismatch events and emit residency-flip metrics to SLO dashboard.
- Postmortem to be authored in Confluence after full rollout; link will be added here.
Current status: In Progress (canary rollback successful; global rollback/patch scheduled).
